comparison.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus cut copper tubing at a mark using a screw-feed orbiting cutter.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve controlled screw adjustment, regrasping, and avoiding disturbance, but the cutter alternates incremental feed with full tool revolutions around a tube; the candidate simultaneously counterholds a screw while tightening its jam nut.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° stop through three cycles; cutting requires full wall penetration without excessive bite, denting, spiral, or mark error.
comparison.reason: The shared screw-control primitive is generic; one preserves a calibrated setting under locknut reaction while the other regulates progressive cutting feed.
